claims.quote: Glucocerebrosidase (GCase), encoded by the GBA1 gene, is one of the lysosomal enzymes responsible for hydrolyzing the glycosphingolipids.

Deficiency in GCase activity (in patients with two defective alleles of GBA1) leads to glucosylceramide storage in lysosomes which in turn results in the development of the Gaucher diseases, a lysosomal storage disorder, while a heterozygous state may be correlated with the GBA1 mutation-associated Parkinson disease.

claims.object_mention: correct conformation of abnormally folded enzymes
claims.quote: One of the proposed forms of therapy for these two conditions is the use of pharmacological chaperones which work by facilitating the achievement of the correct conformation of abnormally folded enzymes.
Studies conducted on the action of this compound have indeed indicated its effectiveness in increasing GCase levels and activity.
